summary: First test iteration for Soneja CRM. Backend: 19/20 pytest cases passed (1 false failure due to concurrent-worker race on shared seeded inventory count - not a real bug; seed inventory verified as 87 via curl). Auth, products, dealers, sales/purchases, payments, inventory auto-adjust (create decrements, delete restores), expenses, dashboard, reports, and staff RBAC (owner-only 403 for staff) all pass. Frontend: login → dashboard renders 87 units in stock, ₹12.54L payable, ₹12,54,200 inventory value; Sales tab shows 4 filter chips (All/Unpaid/Partial/Cleared); New Sale form works (dealer picker with 16 dealers + search, product picker showing stock/cost, qty/rate/amount live update, initial payment); sale creation persisted end-to-end (verified via API list). Sale detail page shows Total/Received/Receivable, payment history, Add Payment form (testID pay-amount). More menu contains all 6 sections (Inventory, Products, Dealers, Expenses, Reports, Staff) with logout. No deprecated Expo packages. Minor issue: after successful sale creation via deep-linked /sales/new URL, the app calls router.back() which logs a GO_BACK react-navigation warning if there is no history; the order is still created. No red-screen, no critical UI bugs.

ui_bugs.issue: After successful create-sale, code appears to call router.back() unconditionally; when navigated directly via /sales/new URL there is no history entry, producing console warning 'The action GO_BACK was not handled by any navigator'. Order still creates on backend. Prefer router.replace('/sales') or router.canGoBack() guard.

issues: Console warning: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"' - RN Web deprecation, low priority.

action_items: (LOW) In order-form submit handler, guard router.back() with router.canGoBack() or use router.replace('/sales') so deep-linked sale creation returns cleanly to the Sales list.
(OPTIONAL) Update RN Web styles to use boxShadow instead of shadow* to silence deprecation warning.

(OPTIONAL) Backend test race: seeded_products stock check ran concurrently with the sale test on the shared 87-unit fixture, producing 85 momentarily. Not a product bug (curl confirmed 87). To eliminate, run inventory-mutating tests serially (pytest -p no:xdist for those, or a session-scoped lock).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py update_product: line 234 `changes.pop('qty_on_hand', None) if changes.get('qty_on_hand') is None else None` is a no-op with `exclude_unset=True` semantics because ProductIn defines `qty_on_hand` as Optional[float]=None but body is a full ProductIn (not partial). PUT /products replaces all fields sent by client; if UI omits qty_on_hand, Pydantic still sets None, then the pop line runs correctly. Consider using a separate ProductUpdate model with all-optional fields for cleaner semantics.

server.py PUT /dealers uses body.model_dump() (full replace), which will overwrite unspecified optional fields with their defaults (empty strings). If frontend sends partial payload, contact_person/area/notes may be blanked. Recommend exclude_unset=True or a DealerUpdate model.
server.py serialize_order age_days: only computed when balance>0.5; cleared orders always report 0 which is fine, but consider preserving age at settlement for reporting.
server.py DELETE /orders reverses inventory but does not prevent double-delete (already handled by deleted_at:None filter - OK).

server.py DELETE /products has no reference check - deleting a product referenced by orders still leaves order items intact (items store their own model/cost snapshots so OK, but sale creation of a deleted product would silently succeed with cost=0 in _create_order line 318 since prod is None). Consider 404 if product not found or deleted.

rca_of_issue: Minor GO_BACK warning RCA: order-form submit handler in app/sales/new.tsx (or components/order-form.tsx) likely does `router.back()` after POST /api/sales returns 201. React Navigation refuses because the history stack has only /sales/new (deep link). Mitigation: `if (router.canGoBack()) router.back(); else router.replace('/sales');` or unconditionally `router.replace('/sales/' + newOrder.id)` to land on the just-created order's detail page (better UX).
